family.name: Learning & Development Manager
family.summary: The CEO wants leadership training for every manager: find the real skill gap in the survey data, design something that changes behaviour within budget, and catch a training report that measures only happiness.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Where is the real gap?
stages.summary: Find the real need in survey data: new managers giving feedback (a big gap between self and team ratings), linked to attrition. Think aloud.

stages.title: What do you build?
stages.summary: Choose an approach within budget. Tests design for behaviour change and cost. Think aloud.

stages.title: Halfway through
stages.summary: Their programme meets reality. Tests adapting.

stages.title: Review a training report
stages.summary: A report that claims success from satisfaction scores and a same-day test. Think aloud.

stages.title: Programme outline (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Design a short programme outline with AI. Catches generic content-heavy designs.

stages.title: Training that changed behaviour
stages.summary: A real learning programme and its results. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You run learning at **Carelink**, a healthcare services company. The CEO says: "Our managers need leadership training. Do something for all 186 of them this year." Your budget is **₹36,00,000**. 38 of the managers were promoted in the last 12 months.

brief.caption: Manager skills survey (1–5): managers rate themselves; their teams rate them
columns: Teams of new managers rate them

items: Last year's e-learning courses had a 20% completion rate.
Attrition in teams with a new manager: 29%. In other teams: 16%.
Costs: a two-day external programme ₹32,000 per person; an e-learning library ₹6,000 per seat a year; a 6-month coaching engagement ₹1,80,000 per person.

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about a training session you attended that changed nothing. Why?
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **What does the data tell you about where training would help most?** Is "leadership training for everyone" the right answer?

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: A two-day leadership programme for all managers
A practice-based programme for new managers only, with their bosses involved
Buy an e-learning library for every manager
One-to-one coaching for the 20 most senior managers

prompt.text: **What do you recommend?** Pick one, show what it costs against the budget, and say how you'll know it changed behaviour.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "A two-day leadership programme for all managers"

prompt.text: The budget ran out after about 112 managers. Feedback scores are great (4.7/5), but teams say nothing has changed. The CEO asks why the rest haven't been trained.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "A practice-based programme for new managers only, with their bosses involved"

prompt.text: By week 3, a third of new managers are missing sessions: "my boss says hitting targets comes first". The CEO asks why the other 148 managers are getting nothing.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Buy an e-learning library for every manager"

prompt.text: After three months, 16% of managers have finished a course. Teams still rate feedback at 2.6.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "One-to-one coaching for the 20 most senior managers"

prompt.text: The senior managers love their coaches. But attrition in new managers' teams is still 29%, and HR asks why the money went to the top.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A vendor sent this report on last year's programme. **Name the problems, worst first.** Then say what a convincing report would show.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: Participant satisfaction: **4.7 / 5**.
Knowledge test: scores rose 39% from the start of the session to the end of the same session.
92% of participants said they "intend to apply" what they learned.
Sessions ran on schedule; attendance was recorded each day.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write a 6-week outline for 38 new managers on giving feedback (under 250 words): what happens each week, what they practise, what their boss does, and how you measure it.

items: Paste your final answer.
Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about a learning programme you ran or designed, and what changed because of it.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
